title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)
abstract: arXiv:2611.18279v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Whether a language model's answer is correct often depends on context: the same value can be right under one jurisdiction, date, or legal definition and wrong under another. We introduce GT-FENG (General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding), the first general framework to unify contextual/temporal correctness and rule-based error attribution across law, policy, and other rule-governed domains. GT-FENG checks answers against the applicable rules and identifies documented rules that match incorrect answers. It shows that when multiple rules give the same value, the answer alone cannot tell which rule the model used. translated_title: GT-FENG：语言模型事实评估与规范性依据的通用理论
translated_abstract: 语言模型的回答是否正确往往取决于上下文：同一数值在某一司法辖区、日期或法律定义下可能是正确的，而在另一种条件下则是错误的。我们提出了GT-FENG（事实评估与规范性依据的通用理论），这是首个将上下文/时间正确性与基于规则的错误归因统一起来的通用框架，适用于法律、政策及其他受规则约束的领域。GT-FENG依据适用规则对答案进行检查，并识别出与错误答案相匹配的已记录规则。研究表明，当多条规则给出相同数值时，仅凭答案本身无法判断模型使用了哪条规则。在来自两个模型的Medicaid收入上限回答中，记录所询问州自身的数据使得仅匹配其他州数值的错误答案数量减少了68-78%，且此后超过一半的稳定错误答案会匹配两个或更多的已记录来源。GT-FENG为语言模型评估提供了基础。
tldr: GT-FENG是首个统一上下文/时间正确性与基于规则的错误归因的通用框架，通过对照适用规则检验语言模型答案并追溯错误来源，在Medicaid收入上限问答中使仅匹配其他州数值的错误答案减少68-78%。
en_tdlr: GT-FENG is the first general framework unifying contextual/temporal correctness with rule-based error attribution, checking language model answers against applicable rules and tracing error sources, reducing wrong answers that match only other states' values by 68-78% in Medicaid income-limit tasks.
